items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: that's the first time I really had the courage to play along with Bix and play the second part

ctx.x: And, uh, I wasn't so far behind in those days either. But, we used to go to this big fat lady--- she lived in not Walnut Hills --but Price Hill and that was quite a ways; it was a big, big hill in Cincinnati and we used to go up there and buy the gin for a dollar a pint and sometimes, we'd each buy ten or twelve depending on how much money we had of those pints. But, during that time, I played a lot of things I never had the courage to play with-- the cornet along

side of Vicks at that point because I certainly wasn't anything near that. But, I could play the mellophone and I could play the trombone parts on the mellophone - and, so, Carl would get his banjo out and Bix get his horn out and we're sitting in the car drinking this terrible bathtub gin and I'd play the mellophone and I wish we had-- I kind of wish there was tapes in those days because we played some very pretty little things together.

items.title: "Wild" Bill Davison Interview
items.q: And, well, Bix for instance, and those kind of guys

ctx.x: My first band? Yeah Well, In Defiance, where I was born It was a very fine band too I mean, it really was a good jazz band for those days It was called the Ohio Lucky Seven And it's just too bad that we didn't record for Jeanette in those days Because we did have it down pretty good, you know And that's why I always laugh when someone said, you know They always say, well, if you don't come from New Orleans Or if you don't come from certain parts of the country, you're not supposed to play But there were, some of…
Do you suppose Bix used records as you did?
